title: A Close Shave
format: Display typeface, three weights, 240 glyphs, specimen booklet
summary: A typeface designed for one real job. A condensed display face for a wool shop’s signs and window, spaced so tight the letters almost touch.
coverAlt: A wool shop window lettered in a narrow typeface with letters nearly touching

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Wool is sold by the inch, so every inch of the window counts. The letters are narrow and set almost touching, and a small notch where they meet keeps each one readable from across the street.

blocks.label: Drawing. Early letters drawn with a broad marker, then traced and rebuilt as outlines.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: I started with the six letters in the shop’s name and grew the alphabet from them. Spacing took longer than drawing. I printed test words at full window size and read them from the other side of the road, then adjusted the notches until no two letters blurred together.

blocks.caption: From the first letters to the spacing test to the three weights.
The specimen booklet, one weight per section.
The shop window, lettered in the heavy weight.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: A typeface is never finished, only released. Next time I would test lowercase much earlier, because the shop’s price tags needed it and I drew it last.
